statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail remains at the upper watch band because the verified Kharg tanker-strike report and continued Hormuz disruption increase reopening-gap sensitivity, while the weekend NQ closure prevents confirmation of persistent Nasdaq price-path failure.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: WATCH; Tail remains below the block threshold. Stress is extreme from Gulf, oil, and rate risks, but no live Nasdaq continuation or failed-retracement structure is observable during the weekend closure.
headline: Kharg tanker strike keeps weekend Nasdaq Tail at WATCH
body: Reuters reports that an Iranian tanker near Kharg Island was hit, with Tasnim attributing the strike to U.S. missiles and no immediate U.S. confirmation. Friday's strong payroll report lifted yields, while oil and Hormuz disruption remain material. NQ is closed, so the current assessment contains no live evidence of persistent mean-reversion failure.

lookbackSummary: The prior 24 hours cover Friday's post-payroll repricing, two brief orange Tail episodes during live trading, the transition into weekend closure, and a return to WATCH after the Kharg tanker-strike report. Outside those live episodes, Tail stayed low or watch because persistent Nasdaq mean-reversion failure was not continuously observed.
outlookSummary: NQ remains closed throughout this 24-hour horizon. If no additional verified Gulf escalation or material Hormuz disruption appears, Tail is projected to ease gradually within WATCH as the Kharg headline ages; Stress remains extreme from conflict, oil, and rate pressure, while confidence declines as Friday's live evidence becomes older.
